title: Fallback variant compatibility curation and automated sanity checks
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: As routing policies fall back between model variants across regions and tiers, small divergences in tokenizer behavior, context window semantics, or tooling hooks (function-calling signatures, structured output markers) produce silent regressions for customers. This ticket creates a curated compatibility registry for fallback variants and implements an automated nightly sanity-check pipeline that detects drift and proposes config PRs.

Scope:
- Build a canonical compatibility registry (format: variant -> canonical tokenizer, context_map, tooling_flags) stored in config repo.
- Implement a CI/cron job that runs cross-variant tests per model family: tokenizer tokenization parity checks, context remapping validation (truncation/left/right pad), KV-cache warm-start shape checks, and tooling hook smoke tests (function call schema matching).
- Surface failures in a dashboard and automatically open a GitHub PR with diffs for safe config updates.

Out of scope: automated in-production remapping of live traffic; fully automated deployment without human review.

Approach:
1) Curate initial compatibility entries for the gpt-family and open-llm variants we route most frequently (list in attachments).
2) Create lightweight deterministic tokenizer parity test: sample 1k representative prompts (from anonymized production prefix corpus), compare tokenization sequence and token offsets. Flag variants with >0.5% numeric divergence or any offset misalignment that would break tool-calling.
3) Context mapping test: simulate request routing with varying client-supplied context lengths; validate fallback variant enforces same truncation policy or maps prefixes into explicit "context_shard" metadata.
4) KV-cache shape check: load a canonical KV cache snapshot and assert that warm-started keys line up (length & dtype) and that recomputed attention indices would not exceed variant max-kv-window.
5) Tooling smoke tests: run function-calling examples and structured-output markers to ensure handlers parse arguments identically.

Telemetry & alerts: Failures are tracked in a per-variant time-series metric and a consolidated "compatibility-drift" SLI. Medium+ regressions create an automated Slack alert and create a GitHub PR in the config repo with the proposed compatibility update and test outputs.

Risk & trade-offs:
- False positives cause noisy PRs and review fatigue. Mitigation: require reproducible failures across 3 consecutive nightly runs before auto-opening a PR; include delta summaries and sampled example cases.
- Over-curation: too many bespoke mappings undermines routing simplicity. Mitigation: prefer generic remapping strategies (e.g., prefer canonical tokenizer label where function-calling exactness is required) and document exceptions with rationale.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.

updates: 2026-03-01 - Triage: Added to smart-routing epic after incident #INC-2026-02 where fallback to v2 caused structured-output failures. Assigned to Diego.

2026-03-04 - Spike: ran tokenizer parity for 6 variants across gpt-family. Observed 0.72% token sequence divergence for variant gpt-v2-quant; offset mismatches on 12 samples that break function-calling headers. Decided to prioritize tokenizer parity checks.
2026-03-07 - Design decision: will implement a "3-night confirmation" rule before auto-opening PRs to reduce noise. Registry schema v1 accepted (see PR in attachments).
2026-03-11 - Engineering: implemented tokenizer parity runner and basic context remapping simulator. Test harness documented in configs repo. Unit tests added.
2026-03-14 - QA: ran a 1k-sample smoke across the canary region. Two variants flagged (gpt-v2-quant, open-llm-lite). Next step: curate exceptions and author recommended mappings in config PR.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical registry exists in configs repo with entries for at least 8 production variants
Nightly sanity pipeline runs end-to-end and produces a human-readable test report in the dashboard
Auto-PR flow opens a draft PR with diffs only after 3 consecutive nightly failures
Telemetry captures compatibility-drift SLI and we have alerting configured for medium+ regressions
Playbook created for reviewers describing triage steps and rollback guidance
